families.summary: Mobile-app accessory to the Philips Lumify handheld ultrasound that gives non-expert users real-time probe-manipulation cues (rotate/tilt/rock/slide), a diagnosability quality bar and view detection for ten standard 2D-TTE views in adults; expert sonographers are excluded from the intended users. First cleared July 2023 (K223347, predicate Caption Guidance DEN190040); the December 2025 clearance (K251416) added an image pre-processing step and a PCCP covering model retraining, additional ultrasound systems and additional cardiac views.
families.intended_use_quote: The UltraSight AI Guidance software is intended to assist medical professionals in the acquisition of cardiac ultrasound images. UltraSight AI Guidance software is an accessory to compatible general purpose diagnostic ultrasound systems
families.indications_for_use_quote: The UltraSight AI Guidance is intended to assist medical professionals (not including expert sonographers) in acquiring cardiac ultrasound images. UltraSight AI Guidance is an accessory to compatible general-purpose diagnostic ultrasound systems. UltraSight AI Guidance is indicated for use in two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (2D- TTE) for adult patients, specifically in the acquisition of the following standard views: Parasternal Long-Axis (PLAX), Parasternal Short-Axis at the Aortic Valve (PSAX-AV), Parasternal Short-Axis at the Mitral Valve (PSAX-MV), Parasternal Short-Axis at the Papillary Muscle (PSAX-PM), Apical 4-Chamber (AP4), Apical 5-Chamber (AP5), Apical 2-Chamber (AP2), Apical 3 -Chamber (AP3), Subcostal 4- Chamber (SubC4), and Subcostal Inferior Vena Cava (SC-IVC).
embedded_ai_features: Quality Bar (image diagnosability score, ACEP grade >=3 threshold)
View Detection (No heart / Navigate / Hold position states)
Probe Guidance (rotation, tilt, rock, lateral-medial and superior-inferior slide cues via 3D probe display)
Image pre-processing step (added K251416) to enable additional probes under PCCP

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance. Versus predicate Caption Guidance: runs on Philips Lumify with S4-1 probe on Samsung Tab S6/S7 tablets instead of Terason uSmart 3200t; no auto-capture or save-best-clip features (user saves clips manually in Lumify interface); intended users exclude expert sonographers.

Renamed UltraSight Guidance. 'the main modification introduced is the addition of a pre-processing step, done prior to feeding images as an input to the device' to enable future compatibility with additional ultrasound probes under a PCCP. PCCP modifications: M1 model re-training; M2 expand compatibility with additional ultrasound systems (image-parameter boundaries of applicability); M3 expanded list of cardiac views (with a clinical utility test requiring the clinical outcome be achieved in >=75% of subjects). Supporting text messages now appear on screen regarding guidance cues. Compatible system still Philips Lumify with S4-1 probe and tablets defined in labeling.
notable_flags: standalone bench testing only (no new clinical study)

papers.title: Real-Time Artificial Intelligence-Based Guidance of Echocardiographic Imaging by Novices: Image Quality and Suitability for Diagnostic Interpretation and Quantitative Analysis
papers.key_result: Novice (6 nurses, 3 residents) exams had sufficient quality to assess LV size, LV function, RV size and pericardial effusion in 99.2%, 99.6%, 92.9% and 100%; concordant interpretation with sonographer images in 83-96%; quantitative LV analysis feasible in 83% with r>=0.74.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in breaking the learning curve for echocardiography: a secondary analysis of a multicentre trial
papers.key_result: Nine novices, 159 patients, 954 images: 97.7% met diagnostic threshold (score >=3); BMI had significant effect (P=0.0029) but all subgroups above threshold; experts ruled out LV dysfunction in 99.4% and hypertrophy in 98.7%.

papers.title: Smarter FoCUS: AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound enables novice detection of left ventricular dysfunction
papers.key_result: 496 adults; novices after 4-h workshop using Lumify + UltraSight guidance; adequate views in 95.0% (AI interpretation) and 97.4% (expert); two-step low-EF screening sensitivity 96.2%, specificity 95.4%, NPV 99.8%; validation cohort of 344 with sensitivity 100%, specificity 99.4%.

papers.title: Improving structural heart disease screening: AI-ECG and novice AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound
papers.key_result: 995 adults; nine novices with Lumify + UltraSight guidance; AI-FoCUS feasible in 97.3%; AI-FoCUS alone PPV 95.4% / NPV 98.0% for selected structural heart disease phenotypes vs comprehensive echo.

papers.title: Reliability of minimally trained operator's left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral measurement guided by artificial intelligence: protocol for a multicentre randomised controlled trial
papers.key_result: Protocol only (NCT06486467): minimally trained operator vs expert LVOT VTI measurement, both guided by UltraSight AI to obtain the five-chamber view, before/after 250 mL fluid challenge in ICU patients; planned n=100.

papers.title: National Cost Savings From Use of Artificial Intelligence Guided Echocardiography in the Assessment of Intermediate-Risk Patients With Syncope in the Emergency Department
papers.key_result: Monte Carlo cost model (returned by PubMed 'UltraSight' query): AI-assisted TTE-first strategy estimated to save $815M +/- $260M annually; not a validation of the device.

open_questions: K223347 Table 1 lists the quality-bar test as 312 subjects and 5,800 clips, but the narrative says 'The test was performed on 312 clips' - the unit (subjects vs clips) is ambiguous.
K223347 summary does not state the number of sites in the multicenter pivotal study, nor the number of novice users (Mor-Avi 2023 reports 6 nurses + 3 residents).

K251416 summary reports only that AUC > 0.8 and FPR < 0.2 acceptance criteria were met; no point estimates or CIs are given for the quality bar or guidance tests, and subgroup results are not reported numerically.
K251416 development (training) dataset size is not stated; the 580-subject / 5-million-frame figure comes from K223347 and may have grown.
K251416 PDF pages 5-12 have non-standard font encoding so the pypdf text is garbled; values were read from rendered page images (PDF pages 9-12) - page numbers refer to PDF page order.
Whether the pilot study (61 subjects) was published in a peer-reviewed journal could not be determined.
Which additional ultrasound systems have been added under the K251416 PCCP (company Jan-2026 release mentions handheld, laptop and cart-based systems) is not disclosed in the FDA summary.

families.summary: Deep-learning accessory app that provides live probe guidance, diagnostic-quality view detection, automatic clip recording and best-effort recording for ten standard 2D-TTE views in adults, running fully offline on a tablet or phone connected to a handheld probe. First cleared April 2025 (K242807, v1.1.1, Clarius PAHD3/PAHD/PAL scanners, predicate Caption Guidance DEN190040) with a PCCP for retraining, new ultrasound systems and new operating systems; the June 2026 Special 510(k) (K260780, v1.3.0) added iPhone support and documented PCCP-implemented Butterfly iQ+/iQ3 and iPadOS compatibility.
families.intended_use_quote: The HeartFocus software is intended to assist healthcare professionals in the acquisition of cardiac ultrasound images. The HeartFocus software is an accessory to compatible general purpose diagnostic ultrasound systems.
families.indications_for_use_quote: The HeartFocus software is intended to assist and guide medical professionals in the acquisition of cardiac ultrasound images. HeartFocus software is an accessory to compatible general-purpose diagnostic ultrasound systems. Heartfocus guides the acquisition of two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (2D-TTE). Specifically, in the acquisition of the following standard views: Parasternal Long-Axis (PLAX), Parasternal Short-Axis at the Aortic Valve (PSAX-AV), Parasternal Short-Axis at the Mitral Valve (PSAX-MV), Parasternal Short-Axis at the Papillary Muscle (PSAX-PM), Apical 4-Chamber (A4C), Apical 5-Chamber (A5C), Apical 2-Chamber (A2C), Apical 3-Chamber (A3C), Subcostal 4-Chamber (SC-4C), and Subcostal Inferior Vena Cava (SC-IVC). HeartFocus software is indicated for use in adult patients who require a cardiac ultrasound exam.
embedded_ai_features: Live Guidance (ML model infers probe position relative to target and gives movement cues)
Diagnostic-Quality View Detection (frame-level classifier; blue-to-green triangle; also grades recorded clips)
Auto Record (automatic capture after consecutive diagnostic-quality frames)
Best-Effort Record (retrospective capture of highest-quality clip when auto-record not achieved)

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance (HeartFocus v1.1.1). Also documents intermediate changes implemented under the K242807 PCCP: Butterfly Network iQ+ and iQ3 probe compatibility with algorithm retraining/validation (M1+M2) and Apple iPadOS compatibility (M3). No clinical study; 'No clinical investigations under 21 CFR Part 812 were conducted or are required'.

training_data.description: 'In total, AI/ML algorithms were trained and tuned on 1,483 patients and 1,204,113 ultrasound images.' Collected on patients of varying BMI, age and sex; sites/vendors not stated. PCCP specifies that each new ultrasound system adds at least 20 patients (~270k frames) to the training set. K260780 states Butterfly iQ+/iQ3 support involved 'corresponding AI/ML algorithm retraining and validation' (numbers not given).

validation_data.description: Standalone test set: 290 patients and 361,104 ultrasound images (view detection evaluated on 30,361 images/14 patients; guidance on 270,582 images/20 patients; recording on 211 long clips/34 patients). Clinical study data (240 patients, 120 US + 120 non-US) also used for retrospective evaluation. K260780 Butterfly validation: ~270,000 frames from 40 US + 40 non-US patients.

prior_validations.description: Company/press coverage of the April 2025 FDA clearance describes HeartFocus as enabling novices to perform heart scans after a few hours of training and notes FDA approval of the PCCP; initial US availability on Butterfly Network handheld devices, US commercial launch announced Aug 27, 2025.

Company website states HeartFocus is FDA cleared, now available on iPhone, supports DICOM/PACS integration, and cites the JACC: Advances trial ('100% nurses acquired diagnostic echo in 100% of patients', AI specificity 'greater than 99%'); a separate HeartFocus Link product for cart-based systems was announced May 28, 2026.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Empowers Novice Users to Acquire Diagnostic-Quality Echocardiography
papers.key_result: Prospective international noninferiority study (2 centers, US and France, Nov 2023-Aug 2024); nurses without ultrasound experience using AI guidance: 100% of novice exams sufficient to assess LV size, LV function, RV size and pericardial effusion; parameters strongly correlated with expert exams.

open_questions: K242807 does not state the number of sites or ultrasound vendors for the 1,483-patient training set, nor whether the 290-patient standalone test set was collected at sites independent of training.
Standalone subgroup analyses (BMI, age, sex) are stated to have been performed but no numeric subgroup results are given in either summary.
K260780 summary pages are scanned images (no extractable text); values were transcribed from rendered PDF pages 5-7 - page numbers refer to PDF page order.
K260780 does not give the size of the Butterfly retraining set or per-subgroup results; the 40 US + 40 non-US patient validation set is described only at the protocol level.

Whether NCT05490303 and NCT05265585 (University Hospital Bordeaux) are the algorithm-development studies for HeartFocus is inferred from clinicaltrials.gov returning them for the query 'DESKi echocardiography'; the FDA summaries do not reference them.
CE-mark status of HeartFocus was not confirmed from a fetched source (businesswire and massdevice pages returned HTTP 403).
The Trost 2025 abstract does not give per-parameter secondary results; those are taken from the FDA summary.
